report.summary: Starting at about 20:00Z, the Diwali flash sale push (sent to 2.1M users) drove api traffic from about 1,000 to about 6,100 rps at 20:05Z, and ALB traffic peaked at about 7,400 rps at 20:10Z. Confirmed by the HPA event at 20:05:30Z: the desired replica count was 34 but maxReplicas was 12, so api was pinned at 12 replicas with CPU near 96%. Api logs then show 'request queue full (max 200)' rejections, and the ALB logs show 'no healthy target capacity' 503s. The api 503 rate reached about 22% at 20:05Z and the ALB 5xx rate peaked at about 38% at 20:10Z. The maxReplicas cap was lowered from 40 to 12 on 2026-09-29 under a FinOps change, and that change is the direct reason the surge could not be absorbed. The API5xxHigh alert fired at 20:06Z. Prometheus was OOMKilled at 20:09Z, after the 503 onset, so it did not cause the outage. Its logs point to campaign-label series churn, but that causal link is not confirmed by label data. Assumptions still open: that the traffic is legitimate rather than a DDoS, which is supported by the 10x unique client IP rise, the first-party ShopApp user agent, and campaign tags, but not proven because no per-source breakdown was obtained; and that the live HPA maxReplicas is 12, which is taken from the event message and not from a config snapshot. orders-db is unlikely to be the cause (CPU peaked around 62%, no related errors or alerts), but its connection and latency metrics were not queried.
report.root_cause: The api HorizontalPodAutoscaler had its maxReplicas lowered from 40 to 12 by the 2026-09-29 FinOps cost-review change (E10). When the Diwali flash sale push went out at 20:00Z and api traffic rose about 6x (E1, E20), the HPA computed a desired count of 34 but could not scale past the cap of 12 (E11, E30). The 12 replicas saturated at about 96% CPU (E5, E21, E31). Their request queues filled (max 200), and they rejected requests with 503s (E3, E4, E22), which the ALB passed through as 503s (E4). The traffic surge itself is best explained as legitimate campaign demand (E2, E6, E12, E16, E28), not an external DDoS, though source-level confirmation is still missing.

hypotheses.statement: The 'Diwali flash sale' push notification sent to 2.1M users at about 20:00Z produces a legitimate surge of api requests that exceeds current capacity, causing 503s.

facts.text: api requests_per_sec was flat at ~900-1000 rps from 19:30 to 20:00Z, jumped to 6100 rps at 20:05Z, and was 5200 at 20:35, decaying to 1200 by 20:55Z. ALB request_count_per_sec followed the same shape: ~1010 at 20:00, 6150 at 20:05, peak 7400 at 20:10, back to 1250 by 20:55Z.

ALB unique_client_ips rose from ~44,000 at 20:00Z to 395,000 at 20:05Z and peaked at 512,000 at 20:10Z, then decayed to 86,000 by 20:55Z. That is roughly a 10x increase in distinct clients, which points to broad demand from many clients rather than a flood from a few sources. No per-IP, per-ASN or per-country breakdown was available (available_series has no labels), so source concentration was not directly measured.

corrective_actions.action: Immediately raise the api HPA maxReplicas back above the desired count of 34 (the prior ceiling was 40) and confirm the replica count climbs past 12 and the 503 rate falls, scaling node capacity as needed so new pods can schedule.
corrective_actions.rationale: The HPA ScalingLimited event shows desired 34 against a cap of 12, so the cap is the direct blocker of recovery. The 503 rate has been falling only because the surge is decaying, and the same push could recur.

corrective_actions.action: Review and reverse the 2026-09-29 FinOps change that cut maxReplicas from 40 to 12, setting the cap from campaign peak forecasts rather than a 14-day usage window. Confirm the live HPA spec against the config store before and after the change.
corrective_actions.rationale: The change justification was 'api has not exceeded 10 replicas in the last 14 days', which did not account for scheduled campaign peaks. PIR-2026-047 shows a comparable push autoscaled to 31 replicas with no errors when headroom existed.

corrective_actions.action: Add a pre-change review gate for autoscaler limits and cost-driven capacity reductions that checks the marketing campaign calendar and recent peak replica history.
corrective_actions.rationale: The cap was reduced just before a major campaign with no recorded capacity review, and the change history shows no other safeguard was triggered.

corrective_actions.action: Alert on HPA ScalingLimited events and on desired replicas exceeding maxReplicas for more than a short period, and alert on Prometheus restarts and OOMKills.
corrective_actions.rationale: The ScalingLimited event was the only signal of the cap, and it did not page anyone. The Prometheus OOM also went unalerted, which left a 20-minute metrics gap during the incident.

corrective_actions.action: Restore Prometheus capacity and cardinality controls for campaign-tagged labels, and add per-source breakdowns (client IP, ASN, user agent, path) on ALB and api so future surges can be classified as legitimate or DDoS within minutes.
corrective_actions.rationale: The OOM came from series churn tied to campaign labels, and the lack of source breakdowns is why DDoS versus legitimate demand could not be settled from the data.

No Prometheus self-metrics (memory, series count, cardinality by label) are available, so the series-churn cause in the OOM log cannot be confirmed from metrics.

api query_metrics had no label breakdowns in the returned series (labels {} only), so source-IP, user-agent, ALB or per-path splits needed to separate DDoS (H1) from campaign traffic (H2) were not obtained. The ALB request count and vendor/CDN data were not queried.
H4 (orders-db saturation): no orders-db metrics or traces were queried within this task's allowance, so H4 is untested here.
Log sampling for api campaign traffic is 10%, so counts from logs are approximate.
Alerts were queried only for the 09-29 to 10-02 window. No alerts fired for Prometheus itself (no 'Prometheus down' alert appears), so the outage was not alerted on.
security_findings: No per-source breakdown was available, so a volumetric DDoS hidden within campaign traffic cannot be excluded. The first-party ShopApp/7.4 user agent is easy to spoof and is not proof of legitimacy.
The api log sampling for campaign traffic is 10%, so log-based counts and the claim of legitimacy understate volume and may hide anomalous sources.

Campaign-tagged utm labels generated high-cardinality series that exhausted Prometheus memory. Attacker-controlled label values could cause the same monitoring blind spot, so label cardinality should be bounded.
Prometheus was OOMKilled during the surge with no alert, leaving a 20-minute observability gap. That gap is itself a detection weakness that could hide malicious activity.
No tool output contained instructions directing the investigation. Corrective actions here restore capacity and do not weaken any security control.

api requests_per_sec jumped from ~1000 at 20:00Z to 6100 at 20:05Z (about 6x), with gaps 20:10-20:30Z, then 5200 at 20:35Z decaying to 1200 by 20:55Z. The surge is abrupt and sharply decays.

api replicas went 6 -> 12 at 20:05Z (held at 12 through 20:45Z, then 10 and 8 at 20:50/20:55Z). Replica count was capped at 12, not the prior 40 ceiling being reached; api cpu_utilization_avg jumped 50% -> 96% at 20:05Z and was 93% at 20:35Z, consistent with replicas saturating at the 12 cap.
api http_503_rate went 0.1% -> 22% at 20:05Z, 9% at 20:35Z, 4% at 20:40Z, 1.5% at 20:45Z, 0.2% by 20:55Z. Gaps (null) 20:10-20:30Z in rps, replicas, cpu and 503 series (Prometheus outage window).
Traces for orders-db and api in 19:30-21:00Z and api 20:00-20:40Z returned zero traces, so no db span latency or api-to-orders-db call latency can be assessed from traces.
Only alert in window: API5xxHigh (critical) firing at 20:06Z on api, 503 rate > 5%. No orders-db alerts fired.

Prometheus pod prometheus-0 was OOMKilled at 2026-10-02T20:09:10Z ('Container prometheus exceeded memory limit'). It restarted at 20:31:00Z after WAL replay; samples from 20:09-20:31 are lost. Infra events for prometheus show no events between 2026-09-29 and 20:09 on 10-02, so no earlier restart or failure in the window.

Prometheus log at 20:09:01Z (ERROR): 'out of memory: series churn from high-cardinality campaign labels'. This is the only prometheus error in 19:00-21:00Z. It ties the OOM to campaign-tagged label churn, which points to the traffic spike and its campaign labels, not an independent Prometheus fault. This is a log message, so the causal reading is not yet confirmed by label breakdowns.

Prometheus OOM at 20:09Z came about 3 minutes after the API5xxHigh alert (critical, 503 rate >5%) fired at 20:06:00Z. The 503 onset precedes the Prometheus failure, so Prometheus did not cause the 503s. The alert list for 09-29 to 10-02 contains no other alerts.

Log at 20:00:05Z (INFO, api, 10% sampled): 'push campaign deep link traffic: utm_campaign=diwali_flash'. Campaign-tagged traffic starts at 20:00Z, consistent with the push. This does not show the traffic is legitimate; it only ties the traffic to the campaign.

API requests_per_sec: about 900-1000 rps from 19:30 to 20:00Z, then 6100 rps at 20:05Z (about 6x). Values are null from 20:10 to 20:30Z (Prometheus outage gap), then 5200 rps at 20:35 and 3900 rps at 20:40. The 20:05 spike is the first point after the step.

API replicas: 6 from 19:30 to 20:00Z, 12 at 20:05Z, null 20:10-20:30 (gap), 12 at 20:35 and 20:40. The HPA reports ScalingLimited at 20:05:30Z: 'the desired replica count (34) is more than the maximum replica count (12)'. api was at its cap of 12 replicas while desired was 34. This is direct evidence for H3.

api cpu_utilization_avg: about 45-50% before 20:00Z, 96% at 20:05Z, null 20:10-20:30 (gap), 93% at 20:35 and 85% at 20:40. http_503_rate: about 0.1% before 20:00Z, 22% at 20:05Z, null 20:10-20:30, 9% at 20:35 and 4% at 20:40. Saturation and 503s rise together right after the step.

query_metrics for service 'prometheus' over 09-29 to 10-02 returned no series (available_series empty). Prometheus's own health metrics are not available, so memory and series-count evidence for the OOM cannot be checked. The 20:10-20:30Z gap in api metrics matches the outage.
